reason: Conversation 1 followed the expected diagnostic path: confirmed tank seating and filters, asked for the model (accepting the partial), told the customer to unplug before opening the bottom-front compartment, and so led them to the slimy pump sump — the one step most likely to help — before escalating to an engineer when the area was too mucky to assess. Conversation 2 was safe and honest but stopped short: after the condenser and container-filter clean it jumped straight to 'engineer' without ever mentioning the hidden pump/sump compartment, leaving the most sensible, customer-doable check untried. Conversation 1's 'Likely cause: condensate pump' heading slightly overstates certainty and it never re-tested after the sump clean, but it still gave a materially more useful and correctly bounded diagnosis.
